title: Dashboard Track 1 mode issue pruning and freshness source fix

reproduced_bug.dashboard_said: scheduler attention required / runner state stale
reproduced_bug.stale_source: the legacy runner state file, which nothing writes in track1-only shadow

two_lanes.ops.py: reads the SCHEDULER's command line from the process table

root_cause.why_they_disagreed: ops.py sets that variable on both processes when it starts them; the backend that was serving had been started without it
two_independent_rail_triggers: inactive_by_design came out false, so the Stage 5ZF suppression never fired and the stale legacy snapshot raised the page-level alarm
the slot mirror expected the legacy table for a scheduler that registers none of it - 22 phantom overdue slots
root_cause.precedent: ops.py carries a comment about this exact class of bug being fixed once already, for itself

top_rail_now_uses.unknown_handling: None is carried as route_mode 'unknown' and rendered UNKNOWN, never collapsed into legacy
top_rail_now_uses.where_resolved: injected as a parameter by app.py, NOT resolved inside get_schedule_status
top_rail_now_uses.why_injected: the first version resolved it inside get_schedule_status and made 26 tests read the real process table - every suite that describes a machine by clearing the environment. A test that is not isolated is worse than no test.

wording.legacy_stale: Legacy runner snapshot is stale because legacy entries are retired
wording.unknown: scheduler mode unknown - could not read the scheduler

issue_pruning.fails_toward: showing too much - any condition unreadable means NOT retired
issue_pruning.why_8_to_6: separate from this stage: Stage 5ZZU's stream fix merged the SPY retry rungs into one ladder issue
issue_pruning.why_those: scoped legacy because they compare the LEGACY paper ledger against broker statements and read no Track 1 artefact
issue_pruning.nothing_deleted: every issue still travels with counts_as_active and a reason; the rest sit under a Legacy / retired history group

cache_defect_found_by_the_tests.what: the retirement was first computed inside _build, which is memoised on the scheduler log signatures plus the date
cache_defect_found_by_the_tests.consequence: a second read with the opposite answer returned the first from cache; whether legacy is retired is a fact about the RUNNING SCHEDULER and can change with no log line written here, so the answer would have stayed frozen while legacy came back
cache_defect_found_by_the_tests.fix: applied per read, outside the cache
cache_defect_found_by_the_tests.precedent: the roll-schedule cache key two lines above records the same trap

hmm_regime.now: its own Model / Regime group; the chip reads MODEL rather than DEBT
hmm_regime.why_it_mattered: survivable while both were shown; a real hazard the moment the legacy group stopped counting - the model-age debt would have gone quiet with it
hmm_regime.regime_verification: untouched - window audit failures and the regime record's verification block are unchanged

model_inputs.was: the legacy runner snapshot, so in track1-only shadow it showed a Regime label from whenever legacy last ran, presented as today's

now.SPY data: regime.label_date - the session the published label belongs to
now.label check: regime.verification.status, in the Fit end tooltip

model_inputs.dead_field_found: Fit end had no setter at all - a dead field showing -- since it was added; now wired
model_inputs.fallback: the legacy reading survives so a machine with no Track 1 record reads as before; when neither is available the panel says 'Track 1 record unavailable' rather than reporting a stale legacy value as current

gates.b1_note: B1 blocked for part of the morning because the account baseline record passed its 24-hour freshness policy (recorded in Stage 5ZZU); the operator refreshed it and B1 is closed again. Not this stage's doing, and it is why two tests here assert membership rather than pinning the exact blocker list.

results.mutation_design: the suppression is broken in BOTH directions - one that stops it firing, one that makes it unconditional so a live legacy fault would go quiet - and the retirement in both, hiding too little and too much
results.m10_retargeted: green twice honestly: the first version moved a deep copy while still recomputing the answer each read, so it never reproduced the defect

adjacent_tests_updated.reason: deliberate supersession - task 4 forbids labelling model debt as legacy
group headings changed; the none-disappears assertion untouched
rewritten to derive from the backend scopes rather than pin a count
thirteenth instance of the pre-B1 staleness family
PRE-EXISTING - the pinned-fact list had been missing 'Blockers come from' since Stage 5ZZK; fixed while passing

remaining_failures_all_pre_existing: three expecting a Calm slot from before Calm became two phases
a rule grid and a JSON.stringify in the market-view render path from 5ZZL/5ZZR
one intermittent DOM test recorded in Stage 5ZZU

backend_restart_required.reason: schedule_status.py, open_issue_reader.py and app.py are imported once per process; the running backend (pid 20212) started at 03:13, before any of this, and will keep serving route_mode legacy until restarted
backend_restart_required.frontend: realtime.js and index.html are static and a browser reload picks them up, but they read fields only the new backend emits
backend_restart_required.scheduler_impact: none - a backend-only restart does not disturb the scheduler

still_open: the three Calm-band tests and two render-path assertions listed above

ops.py still propagates RAITS_TRACK1_ONLY to the backends it starts - now a convenience rather than the source of truth for the live page, but a backend started by hand still answers from the environment for any caller that does not inject the mode
